analyst_view.overall: Early view: Real Oviedo changed coach on 9 November, two days after winning 2-1 at Cádiz: one report says Raúl González, the former Real Madrid striker, replaces Julián Calero in his first senior job, with Santi Cazorla possibly joining his staff, and this is his debut at the Tartiere. Girona, relegated from LaLiga last season, are eighth after two 1-0 defeats in a row (at Real Sociedad II and at home to Almería) but still have Vladyslav Vanat and Yáser Asprilla on five goals each.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean higher: Oviedo's last four league games had three, five, four and three goals, and Raúl has asked for a team that gives everything, which points to a front-foot debut. Girona have the strongest attacking names in the division and missed good chances in both recent defeats (Vanat hit the post against Almería).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. I lean slightly higher: Girona will push to end a two-game losing run and have the wide quality (Carles Pérez, Asprilla) to lift their 3.9, while Oviedo should play with intensity in front of a new coach.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.3 cards. I lean a bit higher: Girona picked up three yellows in the first half alone at home to Almería and had David López sent off at Zubieta, and a new coach's debut in front of the Tartiere crowd should bring an intense, physical game.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots and I hold there. Girona's shot count has dipped (eight with ten men at Zubieta, 12 against Almería), but a home side playing for a new coach pushes the other way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target and I stay there. Girona's forwards are the best in the division on paper but have scored none in two games, and Oviedo's attack, without Chris Ramos (cruciate injury), has a centre-back, Carlos Domínguez, as top scorer with five.
